facts.text: In 2016 an octopus named Inky escaped from the National Aquarium of New Zealand by crawling across the floor and going down a pipe to the sea.
At the Seattle Aquarium, a giant Pacific octopus named Billye quickly learned to remove screw caps from jars.
Research suggests octopuses can plan ahead, recognize and remember individual humans, and solve complex tasks.
Most octopuses live one to three years, and females die after their eggs hatch.
An octopus has about 500 million neurons, and more than half of them are in its arms.
The last common ancestor of octopuses and vertebrates lived about 500 to 600 million years ago, so octopus intelligence evolved separately.
Apart from a small beak about the size of a walnut, a giant Pacific octopus has no hard body parts.
An octopus can pass through an opening only slightly wider than its beak, since the beak is its only hard part.
Octopuses are natural explorers, and keepers give them enrichment such as puzzle-like objects.
Aquarists are advised to cover octopus tanks completely, leaving no gaps, and to latch or weigh the cover down.
In November 2021 the UK government said octopuses would be recognised as sentient in law, after an independent review of over 300 studies.
The review found strong evidence that octopuses and similar animals can experience pain, distress or harm.
